locator.text: Display 33.3, p. 33, in the statement of Theorem 4.6

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. First, on the block itself: this is not a display but the wrapped tail of a running-text sentence of part (iii) (“… at X = X_b, n(X_b,η) = (1,0) and / b_s(X_b,η) = 0.”); the layout scan cut it off at the line break. It is a genuine assertion, so it is audited as a claim; the companion clause n(X_b,η) = (1,0) is not part of this block. Second, the Lean statement: logShearB is the paper's b_s with the opposite sign (shearB = -2X U_X/E, the paper's b_s = 2 D_X U/E = 2X U_X/E), so logShearB = 0 and b_s = 0 are the same assertion. Lean proves it not only at the edge but on the whole outer collar: for every 0 ≤ x < outerWidth v, logShearB v.profiles (eta, rightEdge W - x) = 0, and x = 0 gives the point y = rightEdge W = log X_b, i.e. X = X_b. Hence the Lean statement implies the paper's and says more. It is stated for the final modulated profile v.profiles and for every eta ∈ [-1,1], as the paper requires.
